A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same conformal-isometry study of grid cells. Their text, equations, two tables, fifteen figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original grid-cell learning experiments, ablations, path-integration simulations, and analyses of neural recordings from Gardner et al. (2021).

after.justification: v4 retains the original learning experiments, simulations, ablations, and neural-recording analyses, including the supplementary results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The transformation models, losses, normalization, and conformal-modulation procedure are retained. v3 Section 4.3 and Appendix J are reorganized into v4 Appendices H–I. The explicit nonlinear update in v4 Equation 32 expands the existing modulation rule rather than changing the method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic grid-cell learning in a 2D square, path integration with and without re-encoding, and Gardner et al. recordings from rat R, day 1, modules 1 and 3. No evaluated dataset, population, environment, or task is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators: Banino et al. (2018), Sorscher et al. (2023), and Gao et al. (2021). The added Zhao et al. (2024) citation accompanies the path-integration procedure and does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The lattice resolution, displacement limits, model sizes, training budgets, metrics, and 300-trajectory path-integration evaluation remain unchanged. v4 explicitly specifies uniform displacement sampling for the existing loss expectations; this is additional documentation, not a reported revision of the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The assumption ablations, activation-function comparisons, normalization-noise tests, displacement-range sensitivity tests, and topological analyses are retained. Figures 3 and 7–9 show the same evidence; v3 Appendix I becomes v4 Appendix G. The supplementary neural-data comparisons also remain.

E5.justification: Existing standard-deviation reporting, fitted distributions, and the shaded path-integration curves in Figure 13 are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional training-run or seed counts, significance tests, or revised uncertainty-estimation procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: The numerical and graphical results match. Table 1 retains gridness scores of 1.70 and 1.17 for the proposed models, both with 100% validity. Path-integration mean errors remain 0.002 with re-encoding and 0.024 without it; the neural-data scaling estimate remains 13.4. v4's scaled displacement threshold of 0.8 restates the existing local-deviation evidence.

T1.justification: v4 Section 3.1 supplies an explicit derivation showing how coordinate rescaling preserves the assumptions, and Section 3.3 gives the corresponding loss-scaling identity. v3 Section 4.2 only stated the scaling property. The central torus theorems, Taylor-expansion analysis, and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v4 drops conformal modulation from the abstract and enumerated main contributions while retaining the method in Appendix H. It also presents distance preservation as necessary for path planning, whereas v3 described a potential functional benefit. The central claims about hexagonal emergence and model generality remain.

C2.justification: v4 removes v3 Appendix B's specific limitations concerning interactions with other systems and unstudied position- or direction-dependent metrics. Section 3.3 adds an explicit finite-displacement interpretation of the loss. Section 6 replaces the statement that path planning is future work with a broader argument for planning-centered representation learning.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-repository link on page 1, specifies uniform displacement sampling in Section 3.2, and writes out the existing nonlinear modulation formula in Appendix H.2. Hardware, learning rate, batch size, iteration count, and training-time information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Zhao et al. (2024) as a reference for path integration. It removes the additional-related-work appendix, including detailed discussion of equal-spacing and translation-invariance assumptions attributed to earlier models. Much of the positioning remains in the introduction and Section 5, including the discussion of Schaeffer et al. (2023).

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: v4 retitles the paper, revises the abstract and introduction around distance preservation, adds explanatory Section 3.3, moves conformal modulation into Appendix H, and restructures the appendices after removing the additional-related-work and limitations sections. Language editing accompanies these structural changes.

P2.justification: All fifteen figures and both tables are retained with the same substantive displays. Changes include the ICLR title and page-header styling, figure sizing and placement, upward arrows in Table 1's metric headings, and an explicit meter-unit clarification in Figure 5's caption.

improvement.justification: v4 improves explanation of the finite-displacement objective and scaling behavior, makes implementation details more explicit, and adds project-access information. However, it removes substantive applicability limitations and strengthens the path-planning claim without adding supporting planning evidence. With the central results and proofs retained, the clarity and documentation gains coexist with reduced qualification of the claims; a reliable net quality direction is unclear.
